_monitoring_mandate.SILENCE_RULE_READ_THIS_BEFORE_PUSHING: At ~26 runs/day, an un-deduped mandate turns into 26 notifications a day and Ryan stops reading them -- which destroys the mandate's whole purpose. So: notify ONLY on a trigger below FIRING or UN-FIRING, never on routine state. Each position carries a _notify_state that every run OVERWRITES in place. Before pushing, check last_notified_trigger: if the SAME trigger is still the live one and nothing material has changed, DO NOT notify again -- update the timestamp and mark and stay silent. Re-notify only when a DIFFERENT trigger fires, a fired trigger un-fires, or the recommendation itself changes. A position quietly working is not news; the journal and the EOD report already carry it.
_monitoring_mandate.WHAT_A_RECOMMENDATION_MUST_CONTAIN: Never send a bare 'consider selling'. Every recommendation carries: the trigger that fired and its measured level; current mark, bid/ask and the spread as % of mid (this determines what an exit actually nets and on RBRK it is punishing); P/L in $ and %; DTE and the theta burn per day; the underlying's level versus its written invalidation; the specific alternatives with their trade-offs; and a plain-language RECOMMENDATION with a reason. Sent alone, leg two is not 'the short leg of a spread' -- the broker cannot know a long 695P is meant to cover it -- so it is margined STANDALONE as a cash-secured put and demands the entire strike in collateral. Legging destroys the exact property that makes a vertical capital-efficient. A legged CALL spread is worse: a standalone short call is NAKED (cash.infinite=true), banned outright at any level.
